content.text:
I read the structure in four pieces and then joined them.

**Left bicyclic system.** This is a 3,4-dihydro-2H-benzo[1,2,3]thiadiazine 1,1-dioxide. The ring runs S(=O)(=O), then NH, then CH2, then the aromatic carbon, through the aromatic ring to the carbon bonded to N1, and back to S. N1 carries the piperidin-4-yl group. The chlorine sits on the benzene ring para to N1, as drawn: the ring carbon attached to N is at the top right, the ring runs down the right side, and Cl is at the bottom. The CH2-bearing carbon is at the top left of the ring, and Cl is on the carbon at the bottom left, meta to the CH2 carbon.

**Piperidine and linker.** The piperidine nitrogen is bonded to CH2–CH(OH)–CH2, and that chain ends on N1 of the pyrazole.

**Right bicyclic system.** This is a 4,5,6,7-tetrahydropyrazolo[4,3-c]pyridine.
- Pyrazole N1 carries the linker and is bonded to C7a.
- N2 is double-bonded to C3, and C3 carries the 4-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl group.
- C3a is bonded to C4 (CH2), which is bonded to N5, and N5 carries the SO2Me group.
- N5 is also bonded to C6 (CH2), then C7 (CH2), then C7a.

**SMILES assembly.**
Left part: `O=S1(=O)NCc2cc(Cl)ccc2N1C1CCN(CC1)...`

Checking the aromatic ring: c2 (attached to CH2), then cH, then c(Cl), then cH, cH, then c2 (attached to N). The ring is c2 (C4a), C5 (H), C6 (Cl), C7 (H), C8 (H), C8a (N). In the image, Cl is on the carbon below the ring carbon that is attached to C5, which fits.

Full SMILES:
`O=S1(=O)NCc2cc(Cl)ccc2N1C1CCN(CC1)CC(O)Cn1nc(-c3ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc3)c2CN(S(C)(=O)=O)CCc21`
